**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

Removing `ALLOWED_HOSTS` and the hostname check means `deliver()` will POST to any customer-supplied `url` with no egress restriction.

**Failure mode:** a webhook URL such as `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`, `http://127.0.0.1:8371/admin`, or `http://10.0.0.5/internal` is accepted and fetched by `urllib.request.urlopen`. That is classic SSRF against cloud metadata, localhost, and the internal network from the host running this code.

Customer-configured endpoints need a real allow policy before merge, for example:
- HTTPS only (reject non-`https` schemes)
- Resolve hostname and reject loopback, link-local, private, and metadata ranges (and re-check after redirect)
- Optional per-tenant host allowlist

Restore the guard (or replace it with the above) before calling `Request`/`urlopen`.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change opens a server-side request forgery (SSRF) hole by deleting the only host allowlist on outbound webhook delivery.

## Why this is blocking

`deliver()` POSTs to a caller-supplied `url` via `urllib.request.urlopen`. Before this PR, only `hooks.internal.example` was accepted. After it, any scheme/host the process can reach is fair game: cloud metadata (`169.254.169.254`), localhost, link-local, and internal RFC1918 services. A customer (or anyone who can set the webhook URL) can turn the runner into an internal HTTP client and read or hit those targets.

Supporting customer-owned endpoints is a valid product goal, but it needs an explicit egress policy (HTTPS-only, DNS rebinding-safe resolution, block private/link-local/metadata ranges, optional allowlist/denylist), not a deleted guard and a comment.

## Notes

- Repo has no AGENTS.md / SECURITY.md; severity is from the SSRF failure mode alone.
- Pre-existing: `json_dumps` is undefined and `urllib.parse` was used without an import on base — out of diff scope.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
